stem: A facility changes water sources and laboratory data show the new source contributes substantially different mineral content. What is the best nutrition response?
choices: Keep the fertilizer recipe unchanged because source-water minerals contribute little once concentrated nutrients are diluted into the irrigation tank
Account for the new source-water contribution when evaluating the complete nutrient program instead of assuming the old recipe produces the same final chemistry
Increase each fertilizer component proportionally to the source-water mineral change so the final solution retains the same nutrient ratios as the previous source
Use the new source-water pH as the primary adjustment variable because pH provides enough information to infer the concentration of dissolved mineral nutrients
rationale: Source water can contribute dissolved minerals and alter the starting ionic load. Nutrient programs should be evaluated as a complete system that includes source-water chemistry.
